@graph.description: Does any curated species-level fungal trait predict the presence or absence of the divergent fungal actin, which would suggest a function for it?
@graph.nrr:successCriteria: A trait whose evolutionary history is better explained by a model correlated with divergent actin presence, or a continuous trait with a slope significantly different from zero.

nrr:applicabilityConditions.proteinFamily: structurally divergent fungal actins, defined as ProteinCartography clusters LC04, LC11 and LC14
nrr:applicabilityConditions.absenceDefinition: a species was treated as lacking a DFA if it had no DFA hit and also had more than 6,000 proteins in UniProt the criteria are liberal and likely produce false negatives, especially for species with far more than 6,000 proteins, so DFA prevalence across the fungal tree is probably underestimated
nrr:applicabilityConditions.traitSource: Fun Fun: aggregates species-level ecological, cellular and biochemical trait information from multiple studies, including FUNGuild classifications of ecological function and trophic mode
nrr:applicabilityConditions.phylogeny: TimeTree database web interface; the resulting tree represented 85 fungal orders
nrr:applicabilityConditions.unitOfObservation: species, not independent observations; phylogenetic non-independence is modelled explicitly
nrr:applicabilityConditions.statistics: model selection comparing a model in which DFA presence/absence and the trait share an evolutionary trajectory against a model in which they evolved independently, scored by Akaike information criterion where the lowest AIC wins phylogeny-corrected generalized linear mixed model (logistic regression) testing whether variation in the continuous trait accounts for variation in DFA status while controlling for shared evolutionary history; a slope significantly different from zero would indicate a correlation
nrr:applicabilityConditions.note: conclusions are bounded by which traits had usable public data, not by which traits are biologically plausible

nrr:invalidators: a trait panel chosen for biological relevance with usable coverage
a positive control demonstrating the pipeline recovers a known protein-trait association at comparable sample sizes
a DFA-absence call based on genome assemblies rather than a UniProt protein-count threshold

nrr:cost.note: computational study; 853 species in the working set, 102 analysed; no monetary or compute cost is reported

nrr:provenanceNotes: Each trait is recorded as its own finding and the aggregate claim as a seventh, so a naive count of negatives for this study would be seven rather than one.
Every per-trait finding is uninformative for the same reason, so the class negative-no-association never survives into the record even though it is the pub's own framing.

no multiple-comparison correction is reported across the six traits; the discrete tests are AIC model selection rather than null-hypothesis tests, and the two continuous tests report uncorrected p-values
Sample sizes per trait range from 10 to 71 species: growth form 24, trophic mode 63, ascus dehiscence 13, auxin-responsive promoter 71, spore length 10, spore width 10.

nrr:aiUseDeclaration.statement: We used ChatGPT to help write some code.

nrr:confidence.basis: an average of 34 species per trait, traits chosen for data availability, no positive control on the method, and an absence criterion expected to produce false negatives

@graph.nrr:outcomeSummary: for all four discrete traits the independent-evolution model was more likely; neither continuous trait explained DFA presence or absence; no correlation was detected between DFA presence and any trait investigated

nrr:target.label: divergent fungal actin function, inferred from trait association

nrr:effect.metric: traits showing a correlated evolutionary trajectory with divergent actin presence
nrr:effect.comparedTo: six traits tested: four discrete by AIC model selection, two continuous by phylogeny-corrected regression
nrr:effect.note: for all four discrete traits the independent-evolution model was more likely; neither continuous trait explained DFA presence or absence; no correlation was detected between DFA presence and any trait investigated

positive.note: none; the pub does not test the trait-mapping method against a protein family with a known trait association, so it cannot separate 'DFA has no trait association' from 'this method cannot detect trait associations at these sample sizes'

negative.note: no permutation or shuffled-label control was run

nrr:replicates.note: 102 species in total, an average of 34 species per trait out of 36,253 fungi with at least one structure in UniProt

@graph.nrr:statistics: model selection comparing a model in which DFA presence/absence and the trait share an evolutionary trajectory against a model in which they evolved independently, scored by Akaike information criterion where the lowest AIC wins phylogeny-corrected generalized linear mixed model (logistic regression) testing whether variation in the continuous trait accounts for variation in DFA status while controlling for shared evolutionary history; a slope significantly different from zero would indicate a correlation no multiple-comparison correction is reported across the six traits; the discrete tests are AIC model selection rather than null-hypothesis tests, and the two continuous tests report uncorrected p-values

nrr:conditions.absenceDefinition: a species was treated as lacking a DFA if it had no DFA hit and also had more than 6,000 proteins in UniProt

nrr:evidence.label: The results: None of the six tested fungal traits correlate with DFA status

stated: Only six traits were investigated, and they may not include the traits biologically relevant to DFAs; the restricted scope follows directly from limited availability and quality of trait data.
The trait data were not collected with this study's goals in mind and are therefore likely limited in relevance to DFAs.

Trait-data scarcity significantly reduced statistical power: starting from 36,253 fungi with at least one protein structure in UniProt, reliable trait information was available for an average of 34 fungi per trait.

The ability to link a phenotype to DFA presence is limited by the ability to determine DFA absence, which depends on genome sequence quality and coverage; errors in DFA status reduce the ability to identify significant associations.

nrr:evidence.label: Key takeaways
nrr:evidence.quote: No correlation was found between any of the tested traits and DFAs, so the function of this variant remains unknown.

@graph.nrr:note: The authors attribute the null to trait coverage and to errors in calling divergent actin absent. The record adds that no positive control on the method was run, so the null cannot be separated from a method that would not have detected an association at these sample sizes.
@graph.nrr:informativenessReason: no positive control; no negative control; no sensitivity or power statement

@graph.name: working-set definition and trait curation
@graph.nrr:method: a species was treated as lacking a DFA if it had no DFA hit and also had more than 6,000 proteins in UniProt. chosen to maximise overlap between species with trait information and species with known DFA status, and to include biological features for which actin is relevant. 13 species whose DFA status varied across strains were removed after BLASTp and tBLASTn checks proved uninterpretable, possibly from undersampling or noisy assemblies. 28 further species removed for absence from TimeTree.
